# dsh-wsl-first
**English** | 中文
Make DSH reach for WSL first on Windows.
🎯 Have WSL installed? Then use it — don't let the agent default to writing PowerShell.
## Why
On Windows, DSH hands the model `pwsh` as its default command tool. There's nothing wrong with that
in itself, but if the machine already has WSL, that default costs you.
Models write bash more naturally than PowerShell. Their command instincts are POSIX-shaped. Forcing
a switch to PowerShell means translating pipes, quoting, and paths back and forth — and every mistra
nslation is a retry. **Every retry is tokens burned for nothing.**
Output is the same story. Linux commands tend to print tight, plain text. PowerShell hands you table
s and object properties by default, and the same information takes visibly more room.
Paths too. The WSL tool converts `C:\...` to `/mnt/c/...` on its own, so the model never has to thin
The WSL tool converts `C:\...` to `/mnt/c/...` on its own, so the model never has to think about it.
So this plugin does one small thing: it adds a section to the system prompt saying to try `wsl` firs
t. **It grants no capability and disables no tool — it just changes the default order.**
That prompt text only lists tools that are actually registered. If a tool isn't installed, it won't
appear there, which means the model never gets told to call something that doesn't exist. A static i
nstruction file can't do this; it just repeats what you wrote.
## Features

| 🚀 Saves tokens | One less syntax translation means one less retry |
| 🐧 Built for WSL | The model

writes bash, and it runs Linux-side |
| 🪟 Keeps the escape hatch | When you really need Windows-nati

ve, `pwsh` is still there |
| 🔧 Configurable | Prefer bash instead, or name only `wsl` — it's a conf

ig change |
| 🩺 Never lies | Only advertises tools that are actually registered |
| 🖥 Sidebar panel
| A rail entry showing the current first choice, the fallbacks, and whether the section is publishin
rail entry showing the current first choice, the fallbacks, and whether the section is publishing |
## Sidebar panel
The plugin contributes one rail entry (a glyph plus the `WSL first` label). It opens a read-only pan
el showing the routing in force:
| Panel row | Meaning |

| Reach for first | The preferred executor (`preferred`) |
| Fall back to | The alternatives (`alter

natives`, minus any duplicate of the preferred) |
| Last resort | What is explicitly discouraged (`d

iscouraged`) |
| Prompt section | Whether the section publishes, and its `order` |
The panel is read-only by design: the routing belongs to the bundle row in `cordis.patch.yml`, and a
form here would give one setting two owners that can disagree. Change the file and restart the prof
m here would give one setting two owners that can disagree. Change the file and restart the profile.
It reads the row's own override first and the inherited bundle default second — the same precedence
the Host applies to that row.
> **The first enable needs a DSH restart.** The Host caches its client-package verdict per Loader sp
ecifier. If a profile ever resolved a build of this package *without* a client half before resolving
one with it, that negative verdict is cached too, and nothing short of a restart re-evaluates it —
not a reinstall, a page refresh, or HMR. After that restart, later client-artifact edits are picked
page refresh, or HMR. After that restart, later client-artifact edits are picked up by HMR normally.
## Requirements

| **DSH** | `>=0.1.7-rc.2` |
| **Required service** | `systemPrompt` — ships with every standard pro

file |
| **Required plugin** | dsh-wsl-tool — provides `wsl` / `wsl-path` / `wsl-env` / `wsl-doctor`

|
| **WSL** | WSL2, at least one registered distribution, `wsl.exe` on `PATH` |
| **Platform** | An
y. Windows is the motivating case; the router itself is platform-independent |
This plugin registers no tools of its own — it only routes between tools other plugins provide. With
out `dsh-wsl-tool` there is no `wsl` to prefer, and the section renders empty.
## Install

The bundle ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts the routing row process-wide — every agen
t preset gets the section without declaring anything. **A profile restart is required**; the loader
reads its composition at startup.
If the `wsl` tool itself isn't installed yet, get that first:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## DSH version compatibility
`package.json` declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.1.7-rc.2"`.
The plugin declares **no `@deepseek-ai/*` peer dependency** and imports none of their values. That's
deliberate: at startup DSH runs `evaluatePluginCompatibility` over every profile bundle, and if eve
n one peer range fails to cover the running version, **the whole bundle is skipped** — `cordis.patch
.yml` never takes effect, and it looks like "installed but nothing happens". With no peer range to c
heck, that particular failure can't happen here.
If the plugin goes quiet after a DSH major upgrade, check stderr for `skipping profile bundle` and c
onfirm `engines.dsh` still covers your version.
## Known issues
### Toggling the plugin can report an error
Switching this plugin off, or back on, from the plugin manager can fail with one of these:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**This does not affect how the plugin works.** The routing section stays in the system prompt and th
e plugin keeps running — only the toggle itself does not apply, and no configuration is lost.
[该节后续省略]
## What it deliberately doesn't do
**It hides nothing and disables nothing.** The point is that `wsl` gets chosen first, not that `pwsh
` disappears. Hiding a tool changes what the model can do; a routing section only changes what it re
aches for by default.
The hard version — removing `pwsh` from the tool list entirely — is your own profile patch:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Check that row's real id in your live loader tree before relying on it; a wrong id fails silently.
